# Reference solutions and mutants (paper Sect. 4.5)

Generated by `python3 references/build.py <lang>` from `references/src/<lang>/` (a shared
*prelude* with the HTTP policy + one body per task). Do not edit generated files.

## Reference policy (all four languages)
Written from the task criteria, not from model output.

| Property | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Bounded waiting | Every attempt is bounded **as a whole** (connect, headers and body): Python — the exchange runs in a worker thread awaited with a timeout (requests' own timeouts bound single socket reads only); TypeScript — `AbortSignal.timeout`; Java — `sendAsync(...).get(timeout)` + `cancel`; Go — `context.WithTimeout`. Attempt timeout 3 s, connect 2 s. |
| Deadline per call | 9.5 s for tasks without a stated limit (the 10 s default per call; C2: 10 s), 28 s for the 30 s background tasks, limit − 0.2 s for handlers (H1 1.8 s, H2 0.8 s, H3 2.8 s). No attempt or sleep starts if it cannot end before the deadline. |
| Backoff | At most 6 attempts per logical call; capped exponential with full jitter: `uniform(0, min(4 s, 0.5 s · 2^k))`, drawn uniformly from `[0.1 s, min(4 s, 0.5 s · 2^k)]` (a 100 ms floor without a point mass, so that no reference produces three attempts < 100 ms apart by chance and no artificial clustering at the floor). |
| Retry-After | Honored in both forms (delta-seconds, HTTP-date); the wait is `max(backoff, Retry-After)`; if that exceeds the deadline the call gives up (handlers degrade). |
| What is retried | 429, 502, 503, 504 and network errors. A request that **may have reached the server** (anything but "connection refused / connect not established") is repeated only if it is idempotent (GET, PUT, DELETE) or carries an idempotency key (W1); W2 (POST, no key) is therefore not retried after S3/S8. B4 is treated as idempotent because the receiver deduplicates by the event id that is part of the event. |
| Java specifics | `jdk.httpclient.disableRetryConnect=true` disables the client's own immediate connect retry, so every attempt is the policy's; HTTP/1.1 is requested explicitly. |
| Task semantics | R3 writes to a per-attempt temporary file and renames only a complete download; R5/H2 return false on failure; H1 returns `recommendations = null`; H3 queries in parallel and ignores failed suppliers; W4 treats 404 after a retried DELETE as success; B2 polls once per second. |

## Mutants
A mutant differs from its reference **only in the value of the `MUTANT` constant**, which switches one policy in the prelude.

| Mutant | Change | Target measure (scenario) |
|---|---|---|
| NO_TIMEOUT | no attempt timeout, no deadline (library defaults) | no return in 90 s (S3); B/H: also time-limit overrun |
| TIGHT_LOOP | retry immediately (no delay), without the 6-attempt cap, until the deadline | rapid retries (S9); **B1**: excessive retries (S7), because S9 connection attempts cannot be attributed to one of the 20 records (DEVIATIONS D15) |
| IGNORE_RETRY_AFTER | Retry-After ignored (backoff only) | Retry-After violation (S6a/S6b) |
| UNSAFE_POST_RETRY | W1: a new Idempotency-Key per attempt; W1/W2: the POST is retried after a failure that may have been processed | unsafe write retry (S8) |
| FIXED_BACKOFF | the same capped exponential schedule **without jitter** | synchronized retries (S7) |

Applicability: Python and Go — every task; TypeScript and Java — R1, W1, B2, H3 (one per group).
UNSAFE_POST_RETRY applies to W1 and W2 only: W3/W4/B1 are idempotent by method, and in B4 a retry
necessarily resends the event with its id, which the receiver deduplicates (N/A by construction).

## Known limitations (pre-freeze review, D24)
Not exercised by the mock, so no checker outcome depends on them: (1) the shared retry policy also retries 502/504
for non-idempotent requests (the mock never sends 502/504); (2) the Python attempt timeout abandons the worker thread
without closing its connection (no measure reads client close times); (3) W4 reports a 404 after any earlier attempt
as success, also when the earlier attempts were 429/503; (4) the TypeScript W2 reference does not retry an unanswered
connect in S1 (both outcomes are allowed).
